description: identity/accounts.sh's PROVEN_SELF_CREATE_RAILS case-statement (lines 44-56) is currently a no-op: PROVEN_SELF_CREATE_RAILS is the empty string (line 30), so the matched arm (`*" $rail "*)`, lines 47-51) can never match for any rail, and the default arm (`*)`, lines 52-55) is always taken — both arms set the identical `status="unavailable"`. The case construct therefore has no observable effect on current behavior; it reads as live branching logic but is dead in practice until a future sprint populates PROVEN_SELF_CREATE_RAILS. This is intentionally documented as a forward seam (comment at accounts.sh:26-29), so it is not a functional bug, but it is a structural smell (a conditional whose both branches currently produce the same outcome) worth flagging under HARD RULE 'no dead code paths'.

evidence.snippet:
if [ "$self_create_flag" = "1" ]; then
  case " $PROVEN_SELF_CREATE_RAILS " in
    *" $rail "*)
      status="unavailable"
      ;;
    *)
      status="unavailable"
      ;;
  esac
fi
